title: Review of lab 1's sporecell3-det-twin (SI): fresh seeds 7 and 8 of sporecell3-det give discrete membrane cells of two core kinds that condense from random particles by t~8 and persist at bounded size (6 and 13 persistent tracks); no division in t=200
summary: First labkit packs of threads/particle-life/worlds/sporecell3-det/world.py on fresh seeds 7 and 8 (128^2, t=200, default parameters). From uniformly random particles (t=0) membrane-wrapped cells (pink) condense by t~8-17, and by t~52-69 their cores resolve into two kinds (kind 0 orange, kind 1 green) that persist as round cells while the food is consumed (pack8/sheet.png). Seed 7: 12 tracks, 6 persistent, 9 cells at the end, 0 splits; seed 8: 16 tracks, 13 persistent, 13 cells at the end, 0 splits; max 1.7-2.3 body lengths moved.

observations.S: pack8/sheet.png t=0: random particles over the whole domain; cells by t=8
observations.I: pack8/sheet.png t=60-200: 13 discrete cells of two kinds at bounded size; FACTS 13 persistent tracks

verdicts.limitation: Default world parameters and duration (t=200); the 'det-twin' arm pairing lab 1 used is not encoded in world.py, so I tested only S and I. No division appeared in t=200, so nothing about reproduction or selection is supported by these runs.
